basis: Cortical malformation defines disease; persistent contractures and distal arthrogryposis occur in 30-79%.
Intellectual disability and a defining marfanoid skeletal phenotype; facial dysmorphism does not establish additional organ damage.
Defining limb and skeletal abnormalities; ptosis in 9/16 and developmental delay in 5/13. Endocrine findings in isolated observations do not establish common involvement.
Malignant neoplasm of skeletal-muscle lineage; anatomical sites vary across this umbrella.
Brachydactyly, symphalangism, scoliosis and foot deformities define a skeletal disorder.
Congenital cranial nerve dysfunction with facial palsy; pinna morphology alone does not establish functional ear disease.
Explicitly defined by perinatal hepatocellular injury.
Congenital contractures and skeletal abnormalities with defining congenital heart defects or cardiomyopathy.
Gonadal sex cord-stromal neoplasm arising from Sertoli/Leydig cell lineages, representing the hormonal compartment of the ovary.
Congenital digit shortening and syndactyly; dysostosis and brachydactyly ancestors establish skeletal involvement.
Cystine storage with defining renal and damaging ocular disease; rickets occurs in 80-99%. Neurologic abnormalities are only occasional.
Developmental impairment in 5/5; joint hypermobility in 2/2 with limb deformities supports musculoskeletal involvement. Isolated other-organ findings lack reliable prevalence.
Name indicates lower-lip cleft and canthal/chorioretinal abnormalities; no definition or detailed phenotype evidence is supplied.
Interferonopathy with destructive encephalopathy; hypertension and hypothyroidism each affect 5/16 (~31%). Reported renal failure and hepatic abnormalities are below 30%.
Persistent injury of the brachial plexus, a peripheral nerve structure.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability are shared across chromosome 18p and 18q deletions; other organ abnormalities vary by deleted region.
Defined by hypopharyngeal papillomata, congenital external-ear malformations and microstomia; evidence is limited to one patient or family.
Carcinoma originates in ureteral epithelium; the urinary tract belongs to the renal axis.
Skeletal myopathy caused by an intrinsic metabolic shuttle defect.
Inherited factor VIII hyperactivity is a coagulation disorder. DVT and pulmonary embolism are separately diagnosed thrombotic diseases whose risk is increased.
Defining neurodevelopmental and brain abnormalities; foot deformities reported in 2/2. Ocular and cardiac findings occur in about 25%, below threshold.
Eosinophilic inflammatory infiltration directly affects lung tissue; blood or marrow disease is not required.
Focal dystonia defined by involuntary eyelid closure, impairing eyelid function.
Inherited skin and bile-duct disease; dental hypoplasia or missing teeth in 2/3 and intellectual disability in 1/3. Small denominators limit certainty.
Cerebral perceptual dysfunction causes loss of motion recognition; intrinsic eye disease is not implied.
